hints: An XOR basis has r independent vectors and generates 2^r distinct values.
Every distinct XOR appears the same number 2^(n-r) of times.
Reduce the basis so enumerating its vectors by a binary counter gives XOR values in increasing order.
analogy: Independent switches produce distinct XORs; dependent original choices duplicate every result equally often.
example: For [1,1,2], distinct XORs are 0,1,2,3 and each appears twice; the first five are 0,0,1,1,2.
algorithm: Build an XOR basis with distinct highest pivots. Eliminate each lower pivot from all higher-pivot vectors, then list vectors in increasing pivot order. For index t from 0 upward, XOR the vectors corresponding to set bits of t; output that value 2^(n-r) times, stopping after k outputs. Cap the multiplicity at k to avoid overflow.
correctness: The reduced vectors have unique pivot bits and zero at every other pivot, so the highest differing counter bit determines the ordering of their XORs. The linear map from 2^n subsets onto the rank-r span has a kernel of size 2^(n-r), giving equal multiplicity.
complexity: For n values, B bits and k outputs, O(nB+B^2+kB) time and O(B) extra space excluding output.
